easy.def: A sea animal with a hard shell and big claws.
examples: A crab walked on the sand.
The crab has claws.
We saw a crab.

more.def: A sea animal with a flat, hard shell, ten legs and two large pincers.
examples: A crab scuttled sideways across the sand.
The crab hid under a rock.
Crabs have two big claws.

easy.def: To break without falling apart.
examples: The glass cracked.
The ice cracked.
I cracked an egg.

more.def: To break so that lines appear but the pieces stay together.
examples: The glass cracked when it fell.
The ice on the pond began to crack.
She cracked an egg into the bowl.

easy.def: A thin line in something that is split.
examples: There is a crack in the cup.
The crack in the wall is long.
A crack in the ice.

more.def: A thin line or gap where something has split.
examples: There is a crack in the window.
Water leaked through a crack in the wall.
A small flower grew from a crack in the sidewalk.

easy.def: A thin, dry bread snack.
examples: I eat a cracker.
The cracker is crunchy.
We had cheese and crackers.

more.def: A thin, crisp bit of baked bread that is eaten as a snack.
examples: I ate cheese and crackers after school.
The cracker broke into crumbs.
She put peanut butter on a cracker.

easy.def: Something you make by hand.
examples: We made a craft.
The craft is paper.
I like crafts.

more.def: A skill or activity of making things by hand, or something made this way.
examples: We made a paper craft at school.
She likes arts and crafts.
The craft fair sold hand-made pots.

easy.def: A boat or plane.
examples: The craft sailed.
A small craft crossed the lake.
The craft landed.

more.def: A boat, ship, plane or spaceship.
examples: The craft glided silently across the bay.
The space craft landed on the moon.
Several craft were docked in the harbor.

easy.def: A sudden, tight pain in a muscle.
examples: I got a cramp in my leg.
The cramp hurt.
A cramp in her foot.

more.def: A sudden, painful tightening of a muscle.
examples: I got a cramp in my leg while swimming.
The cramp went away after I stretched.
She felt a cramp in her foot.

easy.def: Too small and crowded.
examples: The room is cramped.
The car was cramped.
A cramped seat.

more.def: Without enough room, packed tightly.
examples: The room was cramped with six people.
The back seat was cramped.
We slept in a cramped tent.

easy.def: A handle you turn.
examples: I turn the crank.
The crank is on the music box.
He turned the crank.

more.def: A handle that you turn to make a machine work.
examples: I turned the crank on the old music box.
The crank on the well is rusty.
He wound the toy with a crank.

easy.def: A loud sound from something hitting.
examples: I heard a crash.
There was a crash in the kitchen.
The crash woke me.

more.def: A loud noise made when something falls or hits something.
examples: We heard a crash from the kitchen.
The crash of thunder shook the house.
A crash of dishes woke the baby.

easy.def: To hit something hard.
examples: The car crashed into a fence.
The plate crashed on the floor.
The waves crash on the rocks.

more.def: To hit something hard and fall or break.
examples: The bike crashed into the fence.
Waves crash onto the rocks.
A plate crashed onto the floor.

easy.def: A strong box for carrying things.
examples: The crate is wood.
The apples are in a crate.
A crate of oranges.

more.def: A large strong box, often made of wood or plastic, used for carrying or storing things.
examples: The apples were packed in a wooden crate.
The dog rode in a crate.
Workers lifted the crate onto the truck.

easy.def: To move on your hands and knees or very slowly.
examples: The baby can crawl.
A bug crawls on the leaf.
We crawled under the table.

more.def: To move along low to the ground, on hands and knees or like an insect.
examples: The baby crawled across the rug to reach the toy.
A caterpillar crawled up the stem.
Traffic crawled along the road in the snow.

easy.def: Very silly or wild.
examples: What a crazy hat!
The dog did a crazy dance.
That is a crazy idea.

more.def: Very silly, wild, or unusual in a funny or surprising way.
examples: The clown wore a crazy hat with a flower on top.
It was a crazy day, with snow in the morning and sun by lunch.
My cousin has a crazy plan to build a boat out of boxes.

easy.def: The thick, rich part of milk.
examples: I put cream in my pudding.
Cream is thick.
Whipped cream sits on the pie.

more.def: The thick, rich part of milk that rises to the top.
examples: Cream is used to make butter.
She poured cream over the berries.
We put whipped cream on the pie.

easy.def: A soft, thick lotion.
examples: Rub cream on your skin.
Sun cream protects you.
Dad put cream on the bite.

more.def: A soft, thick lotion that you rub on the skin.
examples: Mom put cream on my dry hands.
Put on sun cream before you swim.
The nurse gave me cream for the rash.

easy.def: To make something new.
examples: Let's create a picture with paint.
We create a castle from sand.
Bees create honey.

more.def: To make or invent something that did not exist before.
examples: The students created a model of the solar system.
The author created a whole new world in her book.
Wind and water created the shapes in these rocks.

easy.def: Something someone made.
examples: The sand castle is my creation.
The painting is her creation.
The creation is new.

more.def: Something that someone has made, or the act of making it.
examples: The sand castle was my creation.
The artist was proud of her creation.
The creation of the new park took a year.

easy.def: Good at making new things or ideas.
examples: She is a creative artist.
The creative boy made a robot.
That is a creative idea.

more.def: Able to think of new ideas or make new things.
examples: She is a creative artist who paints with unusual colors.
That was a creative way to use a box.
The class came up with a creative game.

easy.def: An animal.
examples: A tiny creature ran under the leaf.
A snail is a slow creature.
What creature made these tracks?

more.def: Any living animal, real or imaginary.
examples: Strange creatures live at the bottom of the ocean.
The tide pool was full of tiny sea creatures.
The dragon is a creature found only in stories.

easy.def: Praise for something you did.
examples: She got credit for the idea.
You deserve credit.
He gets the credit.

more.def: Praise or thanks that someone gets for what they did.
examples: The coach gave her credit for the winning plan.
You deserve credit for finishing the project.
The whole team shared the credit.

easy.def: A way to pay later.
examples: Dad bought it on credit.
I paid with a credit card.
The shop offers credit.

more.def: A way of buying something now and paying for it later.
examples: They bought the couch on credit.
He used a credit card to pay for the tickets.
The store lets you buy on credit.

easy.def: A small stream.
examples: We played by the creek.
The creek is shallow.
A frog sat by the creek.

more.def: A small, narrow stream of water.
examples: We waded in the shallow creek.
A creek ran behind the house.
The creek flowed into the river.

easy.def: To move slowly and quietly.
examples: The cat will creep up on the mouse.
I crept down the stairs.
The fog crept in.

more.def: To move slowly and quietly, often close to the ground.
examples: The cat crept toward the bird.
I crept down the stairs so I would not wake the baby.
Vines creep up the wall.

related.def: A plant that creeps along a wall or the ground.

easy.def: Strange and a little scary.
examples: The old house is creepy.
The dark forest was creepy.
A creepy sound came from the attic.

more.def: Strange in a way that makes you feel a little scared.
examples: The empty house looked creepy at night.
A creepy noise came from the closet.
The fog made the forest feel creepy.

easy.def: A group of people who work together.
examples: The ship has a crew.
A road crew fixed the street.
The crew worked hard.

more.def: A group of people who work together, especially on a ship, plane or job.
examples: The ship's crew raised the sails.
A road crew repaired the broken street.
The film crew set up the cameras.

easy.def: A small bed for a baby.
examples: The baby is in the crib.
The crib has bars.
The crib is by the window.

more.def: A small bed with high sides for a baby.
examples: The baby slept in her crib.
The crib has tall bars on each side.
Mom put the baby down in the crib.

easy.def: A small jumping insect that makes a chirping sound.
examples: A cricket chirped at night.
I heard a cricket.
The cricket jumped.

more.def: A small jumping insect that makes a chirping sound by rubbing its wings together.
examples: A cricket chirped in the grass all night.
We listened to the crickets sing on the summer evening.
The cricket hopped away when I tried to catch it.

easy.def: A game played with a bat and a ball by two teams.
examples: They play cricket in England.
My uncle loves cricket.
We played cricket.

more.def: A ball game played by two teams of eleven players with bats, popular in England and many other countries.
examples: They play cricket on the village green in England.
A cricket bat is flat on one side.
My uncle taught me how to bowl in a game of cricket.

easy.def: Something bad that breaks the law.
examples: Stealing is a crime.
The detective solved the crime.
It is a crime to take things that are not yours.

more.def: An act that breaks the law and can be punished.
examples: Stealing a bike is a crime.
The detective in the book solved the crime.
The town has very little crime.

easy.def: A person who did a crime.
examples: The detective hunted the criminal.
The criminal ran away.
A criminal stole the bike.

more.def: A person who has done something against the law.
examples: The police caught the criminal.
The criminal was sent to court.
The detective chased the criminal.

easy.def: To make small lines or folds, or to make a crackling sound.
examples: The paper crinkles in my hand.
He crinkled the wrapper.
Her nose crinkled when she smiled.

more.def: To form small folds or ridges, often with a light crackling noise.
examples: The bag crinkled loudly when I reached in for a chip.
She crinkled her nose at the smell of the old cheese.
The old map crinkled at the edges as he opened it.

easy.def: A small line or fold in something.
examples: There is a crinkle in the paper.
A crinkle was in her nose.
The foil had a crinkle.

more.def: A small fold or wrinkle in paper, cloth or skin.
examples: He smoothed out the crinkle in the corner of the page.
Little crinkles formed around her eyes when she laughed.
The bag of leaves made a crinkle sound under my shoe.

easy.def: A time of great danger or trouble.
examples: The flood was a crisis.
The town faced a crisis.
The crisis ended.

more.def: A time of great trouble or danger when something must be done.
examples: The flood put the town in crisis.
The teacher stayed calm during the crisis.
A crisis can bring neighbors together.

easy.def: A person who tells what they think of a book or movie.
examples: The critic liked the movie.
A critic wrote a review.
The critic gave the play praise.

more.def: A person who judges books, movies or plays and tells what is good or bad about them.
examples: The critic liked the movie and gave it a good review.
A food critic visited the restaurant.
The critics praised the new play.

easy.def: Very important.
examples: The first step is critical.
Water is critical for plants.
Sleep is critical.

more.def: Extremely important, because a lot depends on it.
examples: Water is critical for plants to grow.
The next few minutes are critical for the team.
It is critical to wear a seat belt.

easy.def: Saying what is wrong with something.
examples: He was critical of my drawing.
The teacher was not critical.
A critical remark hurt her.

more.def: Pointing out faults or mistakes in something.
examples: He was critical of my drawing and said it was messy.
A critical remark hurt her feelings.
The reviewer was critical of the movie.

easy.def: To say what you think is wrong with something.
examples: Do not criticize your friend.
She criticized my drawing.
He criticizes the movie.

more.def: To say what you think is bad or wrong about someone or something.
examples: It is not kind to criticize a friend's work without helping.
The reviewer criticized the movie for being too long.
My coach criticizes my kick, but then shows me how to fix it.

easy.def: Not straight.
examples: The picture is crooked.
A crooked path.
The tree is crooked.

more.def: Bent or twisted, not straight.
examples: The picture on the wall is crooked.
A crooked path wound up the hill.
The old tree had a crooked trunk.

easy.def: Plants that farmers grow.
examples: Corn is a crop.
The farmer grows a crop.
The crop is ready.

more.def: Plants such as corn or wheat that are grown in large amounts for food.
examples: Corn is the main crop on the farm.
The farmers gathered the crop in the fall.
Rain helped the crops grow.

easy.def: To go from one side to the other.
examples: Cross the street.
We crossed the bridge.
Look both ways before you cross.

more.def: To go from one side of something to the other.
examples: The ducks crossed the road in a line.
We crossed the bridge over the river.
Be careful when you cross the street.

easy.def: A mark like an X or a plus sign.
examples: Put a cross on the map.
She drew a cross.
There is a cross on the church.

more.def: A shape made by two lines that go across each other.
examples: The pirate map showed a red cross.
The church had a tall cross on its roof.
Draw a cross in the box to show your answer.

easy.def: Angry.
examples: Dad was cross.
The cross cat hissed.
She is cross with me.

more.def: Annoyed or a little angry.
examples: He was cross because his sister borrowed his bike.
The cross cat hissed at the dog.
Do not be cross with me.

easy.def: A big black bird.
examples: A crow is black.
The crow sat on a pole.
Crows caw.

more.def: A large black bird that has a loud, harsh call.
examples: A crow sat on the fence.
Crows are smart birds.
The crow cawed from the top of the tree.

easy.def: To make a loud call, like a rooster.
examples: The rooster crows.
The rooster crowed at dawn.
I heard it crow.

more.def: To make a loud call, like a rooster does in the morning.
examples: The rooster crows at dawn.
The rooster crowed when the sun came up.
We woke up when the rooster began to crow.

easy.def: A lot of people together.
examples: A crowd came to the show.
The crowd cheered.
The crowd was big.

more.def: A large group of people together in one place.
examples: A crowd gathered to watch the parade.
The crowd cheered when the band played.
We got lost in the crowd.

easy.def: Full of people.
examples: The bus is crowded.
The beach was crowded.
The room is crowded.

more.def: Filled with too many people or things.
examples: The bus was crowded after school.
The beach is crowded in summer.
The crowded room was hot and noisy.

easy.def: A shiny hat that a king or queen wears.
examples: The queen wears a crown.
The crown is gold.
The prince has a crown.

more.def: A circle or hat made of gold and jewels, worn by a king or queen.
examples: The queen wore a golden crown.
The king's crown was covered in jewels.
The princess put the crown on her head.

easy.def: Very, very important.
examples: Water is crucial for plants.
It is crucial to look both ways.
Sleep is crucial.

more.def: Extremely important, because everything depends on it.
examples: Water is crucial for every plant and animal on Earth.
It was crucial that we arrive before the show started.
She scored the crucial goal in the last minute of the game.

easy.def: Mean and hurting others on purpose.
examples: It is cruel to hurt animals.
The cruel king was unkind.
That was a cruel thing to say.

more.def: Causing pain or sadness to others on purpose, and not caring.
examples: It is cruel to hurt an animal.
The cruel king took food from the poor.
The frost was cruel to the new flowers.

easy.def: A trip on a big ship.
examples: We went on a cruise.
The cruise was fun.
The cruise ship is huge.

more.def: A holiday trip on a large ship that visits many places.
examples: We went on a cruise to the islands.
The cruise ship stopped at three ports.
They took a cruise down the river.

easy.def: To move along smoothly.
examples: The car cruises.
The ship cruised.
The bird cruised.

more.def: To travel along at a steady, smooth speed.
examples: The car cruised along the highway.
The eagle cruised over the valley.
The boat cruised across the bay.

easy.def: A tiny bit of bread, cake or cookie.
examples: There are crumbs on the table.
A crumb fell on the floor.
The birds ate the crumbs.

more.def: A tiny piece that has broken off bread, cake or cookies.
examples: There were cracker crumbs all over the floor.
The birds gathered to eat the bread crumbs we threw.
He brushed the crumbs off the table into his hand.

easy.def: To chew something that makes a noise.
examples: I crunch an apple.
The snow crunched.
She crunched the chips.

more.def: To crush or chew something hard so that it makes a noise.
examples: I crunched an apple.
The snow crunched under my boots.
She crunched the crackers.

easy.def: A loud, crackling sound.
examples: I heard a crunch.
The crunch of leaves.
The crunch was loud.

more.def: The sharp sound of something being crushed.
examples: I heard the crunch of gravel.
The apple had a loud crunch.
We heard a crunch as the car ran over a twig.

easy.def: A long, strong effort to make something better.
examples: She led a crusade to clean the park.
The class began a crusade for a new playground.
His crusade was to save the old tree.

more.def: A long, hard-working effort by people to change something they believe is important.
examples: The students started a crusade to keep the river clean.
Her crusade for safer streets lasted for many years.
The doctor led a crusade to get clean water to every village.

easy.def: To squash something.
examples: Do not crush the can.
The rock crushed the box.
She crushed the leaves.

more.def: To press something so hard that it is broken or flattened.
examples: The truck crushed the empty can.
She crushed the leaves in her hand.
Be careful not to crush the flowers.

easy.def: To have tears come from your eyes.
examples: The baby cries.
I cried when I fell.
She cried at the sad movie.

more.def: To let tears fall from your eyes because you are sad, hurt or very happy.
examples: The baby cried until Mom picked her up.
She cried happy tears when her dog came home.
I cried when I scraped my knee on the sidewalk.

easy.def: To call out loudly.
examples: "Help!" she cried.
"Look!" he cried.
The gull cried over the sea.

more.def: To shout something out loudly.
examples: "Look out!" cried the lifeguard.
"Hooray!" cried the children as the circus began.
Gulls cried overhead as the boat came to shore.

easy.def: A hard, clear, shiny stone.
examples: The crystal sparkles.
I found a crystal.
The crystal looks like ice.

more.def: A hard, clear mineral with flat sides that shines in the light.
examples: The crystal sparkled in the sunlight.
We found a purple crystal in the cave.
Salt forms tiny crystals.
